issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner-group follow mode can never be set — the picker POSTs the wrong JSON key, so the backend rejects every follow-mode selection with 400.

Contract mismatch across repos:
- Frontend src/services/partner-groups.service.ts:267-279 setFollowMode() POSTs /partner-groups/:id/follow-mode with body { mode, custom_diet_plan_id, custom_workout_plan_id } — the mode value is under the key `mode`.
- Backend app/routes/partner_groups.py:708 reads follow_mode = body.get('follow_mode'). Since the FE never sends a `follow_mode` key, this is always None, so line 709 `if follow_mode not in _VALID_FOLLOW_MODES` is true and the handler returns 400 INVALID_FOLLOW_MODE for EVERY request.

The sibling scaling-mode endpoint proves the deviation: FE sends { mode } and backend partner_groups.py:741 reads body.get('mode') — consistent. Only follow-mode is out of sync (FE `mode` vs BE `follow_mode`). The mode string VALUES all match _VALID_FOLLOW_MODES exactly (both/diet_only/workout_only/custom_diet_leader_workout/leader_diet_custom_workout); only the wrapping JSON key is wrong.

Blast radius: FollowModePicker (src/components/partners/FollowModePicker.tsx:121-138) is the ONLY caller. Every tap on any of the 5 follow-mode cards fires the mutation -> 400 -> onError toast 'Couldn't update follow mode' -> my_follow_mode stays null. A member who accepts a partner-group invite is routed straight to /partners/:groupId/follow-mode (PartnerInvites.tsx:48) and is physically unable to complete setup: the picker's whole purpose (choose how to follow the leader's plan) is dead. Settings -> Change is equally broken.

Expected: tapping a follow-mode option persists it (200) and the group hub reflects the chosen mode; the diet/workout views scale to that mode.
Actual: 400 INVALID_FOLLOW_MODE on every attempt; a red 'Couldn't update follow mode' toast; follow mode never changes from 'Not set'.

Repro:
1. Be a member of a partner group with follow mode unset (accept an invite, or Group settings -> Follow mode -> Change).
2. Tap any option in the follow-mode picker (e.g. 'Both').
3. Network: POST /api/v1/partner-groups/<id>/follow-mode with body {"mode":"both",...} returns 400 {"code":"INVALID_FOLLOW_MODE"}.
4. UI shows the error toast; the mode stays 'Not set'.

Fix (pick one, keep both repos in sync): change the FE service to send { follow_mode: mode, ... } (matches backend + the follow_mode_changed discord log key), OR make the backend accept follow_mode = body.get('follow_mode') or body.get('mode'). Sending the key as follow_mode is the smaller, contract-correct change.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: the follow-mode picker sent your choice under the JSON key 'mode', but the server only reads 'follow_mode', so every selection was rejected (400 INVALID_FOLLOW_MODE) and members could never finish partner-group setup. Fix: the app now sends 'follow_mode', and the server also still accepts the legacy 'mode' key so already-installed apps work immediately after the backend deploy. Verified end-to-end: tapping a mode now saves and shows as Current.

judge.note: Contract fix in both repos (FE key rename + BE tolerant read); FE 49 + BE 5 tests green; two adversarial reviews clean; scenario capture shows POST {follow_mode:both} -> 200, success toast + Current badge. Backend live+healthy on prod.

Also ties into the in-flight i18n directive: Hindi/Hinglish speech-to-text + parsing is a natural differentiator for the India-focused base. V1 SCOPE: in the Add Custom Meal sheet, add a "Describe it" text field (mic button using the Web Speech API on web / native STT on Capacitor where available, falling back to typed text) -> POST the transcript to a new /api/v1/nutrition/parse-meal-text endpoint -> LLM returns items+macros -> prefill the existing manual fields, editable before save (same edit-then-confirm pattern already used for photo logging). No new logging surfaces, no schema changes to DailyLog. EFFORT: ~1-2 days FE (mic capture + prefill wiring reusing existing food-item form) + ~0.5 day BE (one endpoint, reuse llm_service prompt scaffolding).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Coach-chat outbox replay DOUBLE-PERSISTS a message when the offline gap exceeds the backend 5-min nonce-dedup TTL (or a backend restart clears the cache).

The IndexedDB message outbox re-sends a failed message carrying its ORIGINAL nonce (src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useSendMessage.tsx:190 enqueue on ack-reject; useChatOutbox.ts:31-63 replay on reconnect), and the FE EXPLICITLY relies on the server deduping that replay (chat.service.ts:427-429, useChatOutbox.ts:44-46, useSendMessage.tsx:137-139 -- "a lost ack cannot double-persist"). But the servers ONLY dedup layer is an in-process cache with a 5-minute TTL, cleared on restart (backend.py:15044 _MSG_NONCE_TTL_S=300; _msg_nonce_seen/_msg_nonce_record). Message rows have NO nonce column / unique constraint (backend.py:15180 insert), so once the cache entry is gone nothing stops a re-insert.

The outbox is designed to retry after ARBITRARY offline periods (toast: "We will retry automatically when you are back online" + IndexedDB persistence surviving app close), which routinely exceeds 5 min on mobile -- so the dedup window is far shorter than the retry window it is meant to protect.

Repro A (TTL expiry): send a coach message; drop connectivity in the ~15s window right AFTER the socket emit but AFTER the server persisted + recorded the nonce (common on mobile: background the app / lose signal). sendRealtimeMessageAck rejects -> message enqueued to outbox. Reconnect >5 min later -> replayOutbox re-sends with the same nonce -> _msg_nonce_seen misses (entry expired) -> message persisted AGAIN + re-broadcast. Expected: replay deduped to one copy. Actual: TWO identical user messages in the thread; if directed_to=ai the coach LLM ALSO runs twice (extra token cost + a 2nd AI reply to the same line).

Repro B (backend restart, even <5 min): same lost-ack enqueue, then a backend deploy/restart clears _msg_nonce_cache, then the FE reconnects and replays -> double-persist. Backend deploys are frequent (auto-deploy directive).

Root cause: dedup window (5 min, process-local, restart-volatile) << outbox retry window (arbitrary). Fix: persist the nonce to a Message.client_nonce column with a UNIQUE index on (sender_id, client_nonce) and dedupe at insert (catch IntegrityError -> ack the existing id), or back the nonce cache with a persistent store (DB/Redis) whose TTL matches the outbox lifetime. Confirmed both repos (FE useChatOutbox.ts + useSendMessage.tsx + chat.service.ts; BE backend.py handle_send_message).
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: after going offline for more than ~5 minutes (or when the backend restarted), the app's automatic message-resend could save the same coach-chat message twice — two identical messages in the thread, and for AI messages the coach even replied twice. Fix (backend): every message now carries a unique client tag enforced by a database unique index, so a resend can never create a duplicate — the server just re-confirms the existing message. Deployed and verified live on production; covered by 3 new tests.

judge.note: Root-cause fix (durable unique index + insert dedup + LLM double-run guard); deployed to prod, live schema verified, 3 tests red-before/green-after. Proof is an evidence card (backend fix has no app-screen surface).
